# Compiled kernels in this directory: sources and exact build lines (R3 = kai #151 cb-xa-ftok (tcb2 = #141 r137-ng7 + pjs ROP + kai KFX / ZC-IN, + kai XA3 / FTOK) + ruj PROFUSE-v + ruj MIXR32)

Every compiled kernel this image ships is a `.cubin` in `/opt/s1eng/s1eng/`, and each one sits next to its CUDA source. Each cubin rebuilds **byte for byte** from that source with the build line below, run in `/opt/s1eng/s1eng` (the directory of this file inside the image) with nvcc 13.4 (`Cuda compilation tools, release 13.4, V13.4.92`, `Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0`). Besides the cubins there is one host library, `ftokc.so` (FTOK, section below), next to its C source `ftokc.c`. Nothing else in the image's engine layer is compiled: the rest is Python source, JSON tables and text. The layers below it are the official `ghcr.io/reaxlabs/reax-s1-fast-runtime:1.2.0-rc1` layers, unchanged.

## Host library: ftokc.so (FTOK, kai/cb-ftok)

| library | sha256 of the library | source | sha256 of the source | build line (in `/opt/s1eng/s1eng`) | author | loaded by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ftokc.so` | `2b34d5b4b7b56dfbe38fa57be16ac1005da54b1b64ce886cdb02bc0ea0e224dc` | `ftokc.c` | `1fe352dc6cf510839fff3137387f60aad2a7d30bf9a22b7afbba81d65e76b82c` | `gcc -O2 -fPIC -shared -nostdlib -ffreestanding -fno-builtin -o ftokc.so ftokc.c` | kai | ftok.py with S1ENG_FTOK=1 or an ARMS arm `ftok` (ctypes; never loaded otherwise) |

* Compiler: gcc 13.3.0 (`gcc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0`, Ubuntu 24.04, x86-64). The build line above gives `ftokc.so` byte for byte, in any directory (no debug info, so no path is recorded; the `.comment` section records the compiler version, so another gcc gives a different file).
* Freestanding: no libc and no other library (`readelf -d ftokc.so` lists no NEEDED entry, `readelf --dyn-syms` no undefined symbol), so it loads in the image whatever its glibc. It exports `ftok_abi`, `ftok_put`, `ftok_get`, `ftok_encode`.
* It is named `ftokc`, not `ftok`: an `ftok.so` next to `ftok.py` would be taken by Python's import system as the extension module `s1eng.ftok`.
* What it computes and why that is exact: the comment at the top of `ftokc.c` and the docstring of `ftok.py`; the tests are `tests/test_ftok.py` (ids equal to tokenizers' on every `tail_samples()` tail, 80k adversarial ASCII tails, every 2-character ASCII string, Unicode fallbacks and 1,000,000 validator tails).

## Levers in this image and their authors (provenance)

This image is kai's #151 cb-xa-ftok (the team combination B2 = rgh's #141 (r137-ng7 = pv131mpf + NG7 / NG7T, with rgh's PRON) plus pjs's ROP plus kai's KFX and ZC-IN, then kai's XA3 and FTOK) plus ruj's PROFUSE-v and ruj's MIXR32 (R3). Who wrote what:

* **PRON** (native one-launch GDN prologue: `pron.cu` / `pron.cubin` / `pron.py` and its hooks in `model.py`, `batchfwd.py`, `ntv.py`; `S1ENG_PRON` unset = on): **rgh** (v16). Shipped unmodified, as rgh's code.
* **NG7 / NG7T** (`ngemm7.cu` / `ngemm7.cubin`, `ng7t.py`, `ng7_table_pro6000.json`, the NG7 hooks in `ng.py`, `model.py`, `kprio.py`; `S1ENG_NG7=1 S1ENG_NG7_TABLE=1`): the nsw7l gate|up + SwiGLU kernels are **pjs**'s (e5y); the four tall-tail instantiations, the NG7T table and the s1eng port are **rgh**'s.
* **ROP** (`fcl.py` `ro_plan` / `readout_rows`, `batchfwd.py` `ro_rows`, the RO start-up block in `model.py`; `S1ENG_RO_PAD=1`): **pjs** (e10), on **ruj**'s FCL RO readout. Python only: RO's batched readout runs only at row counts whose cuBLAS GEMV kernel is the per-row reference's (a graph B whose own count runs another GEMV instance is padded with zero rows to a good count, or falls back to the per-row products), checked at start-up by kernel identity and a byte gate on random and near-tie rows; the start-up line `lever used: ROP (S1ENG_RO_PAD)` lists the count chosen for every graph B.
* **ZC-IN** (`zcin.cu` / `zcin.cubin` / `zcin.py`, `BatchLoop._zc_setup` / `_zc_checks` and the ZC branches of the lean and mixed lean launches in `model.py`; `S1ENG_ZC=1`) and **KFX** (`kfx.cu` / `kfx_map.h` / `kfx.cubin`, the `KF_NO_KERNELS` guard and `late` hook in `kf.cu`, the KFX loader / launch / gate in `mx.py`, `batchfwd.py` `mx_kfx_gate`, the per-pair gate in `model.py`, the `fcab.py` pick registry; `S1ENG_KFX=1`): **kai** (#138 kx-zc). KFX instantiates ruj's KF tile (`kf_tile`). kai's ARMS / RAMP / HOST-probe / MIX_RSTEP-arm plumbing ships with them (the ZC hunks share it); it is inert at this image's ENV.
* **XA3** (`xa3.cu` / `xa3.cubin`, the variant / gate code in `xa.py`, the `xa.variant_check` call sites in `batchfwd.py` `check_xa` and `fcl.py` `xl_check`, the `ntv.py` re-check count, the XA3 lines in `model.py` `capture_batch`, the FCAB pick lever `xa3`; `S1ENG_XA3=1`, off unless set): **kai** (kai/rf-xa, ported onto this tree as kai/cb-xa). Derived from rgh's `xa.cu`, which stays unchanged with its `xa.cubin`; see XA3 below.
* **FTOK** (`ftokc.c` / `ftokc.so` / `ftok.py`, the FTOK hooks in `mpf.py` and `model.py`; `S1ENG_FTOK=1`): **kai** (kai/cb-ftok; see the host-library section above).
* **PROFUSE-v** (`onormpv.cu` / `onormpv.cubin` / `onormpv.py`, the `_profuse` dispatch in `batchfwd.py` `_gdn`, the start-up gate block after ONORM's in `model.py` `capture_batch`, the re-check in `ntv.py` `recheck`; `S1ENG_PROFUSE=1`, off unless set): **ruj** (r3). The idea - ONORM computing the GDN value rows itself from the raw qkv rows so that PRON writes q / k only - and the raw-row / halo staging are rgh's dev_profuse (`ffsp.cu`, built on `ffs.cu`'s fused5 body, not shipped); the port onto ONORM's fused5n body, the column-slab conversion, the gate and the dispatch are ruj's. `onorm.cu`, `pron.cu` and their cubins are unchanged.
* **MIXR32** (`S1ENG_MIX_RSTEP=32` in the image config; no code and no compiled file of its own): **ruj** (the setting: fixb, dashboard #132; the knob is the R-grid option `S1ENG_MIX_RSTEP` of `mix_rows` in `model.py`, part of the MX code listed below). With it the 128 -> 192 mixed graphs are captured at every 32-row bin instead of every 64-row one (`slots/R bins {4: 16, 5: 15, 6: 18, 7: 21, 8: 23, 12: 31}`, 124 mixed graphs per lane instead of 71; every 64-grid bin is still captured). The new bins run the same kernels with the same plan picks; MX's `mix_check`, the skx6t gate (240 instead of 160 (N, K, R) keys) and kai's KFX gate (240 keys) check them at start-up, and the mixed graphs' GDN layers run PROFUSE-v like every other packed graph. Unset or `=64` gives #151's mixed graphs exactly. Notes: `/opt/s1eng/levers/mixr32/LEVER.md`.
* **MPF** (`mpf.py`, `S1ENG_MPF=4`), **KF** (`kf.cu`, `S1ENG_2N2560SPLITKPINSMLPDOWNGDNOUTPROJATTENTIONOPROJATTENTIONKV=1`), **skx6 / skx6t** (`skx6.cu`, `skx6t.cu`, `S1ENG_SKX6T=1`), **MX** mixed graphs (`S1ENG_MIX`), **SKR** (`S1ENG_SKR=1`), **MSD** (`S1ENG_MSD=1`): **ruj**.
* Every other compiled kernel: the author column of the table above (rgh: NG3, NG9B, COV9b, RARN, XA, KKT2, FFS, ONORM; ruj: RN, off here).

## kfx.cubin (KFX) and zcin.cubin (ZC-IN)

* `kfx.cu` includes `kf.cu` (with `KF_NO_KERNELS`, sha256 `57d67f979cc642c90c3cae421835930329b55454c13cf633ed55b230674192b3`) and `kfx_map.h` (sha256 `abed2f38e4c4d03d10cc7d773da6d243cb25e157eb74ffb131d72b68f0a609f8`); its build line above, run in this directory, gives `kfx.cubin` byte for byte (md5 `984ae68f99d2992da6d18998c3620b06`, = kai's #138 build). kai's `kf.cu` adds only an `#ifndef KF_NO_KERNELS` guard and a `late(m0, mend)` hook whose default does nothing: `kf.cubin` still rebuilds byte for byte from it (md5 `c539fe299fca6eafc2251051a8f0d5a2`, unchanged).
* `zcin.cubin` here is the nvcc 13.4 (`V13.4.92`) build of `zcin.cu` with the line above (md5 `82d8ad000dd0e1c13263a4d3242e3229`; ptxas: 38 registers, 0 stack, 0 spills). kai's #138 shipped the nvcc 13.0 (`V13.0.88`) build of the same source (md5 `ac2a68a31c60fd6ff7e3d340de05583c`; it also rebuilds byte for byte from this `zcin.cu` with nvcc 13.0.88 from NVIDIA's PyPI wheels in Ubuntu 24.04). Both builds have the same memory instructions (5 `LDG.E.128.STRONG.SYS` + 1 `LDG.E.U8.STRONG.SYS`, 5 `STG.E.128` + 1 `STG.E.U8`) and differ only in the uniform-register setup; this image ships the 13.4 build so that every cubin here rebuilds with one toolkit. The ZC-IN start-up gate byte-checks the shipped kernel on the GPU (random blobs of every meta size in use, both paths, twice, a 64-byte guard), then runs self_check / mix_check on every lane set with the kernel-copied inputs; any failure leaves ZC off.

### XA3 (kai/rf-xa, BACKLOG2 2.4 XA-LAT; switch `S1ENG_XA3`, default off)

* Source: `xa3.cu` (sha256 `bf836985bd3af8c7f7aed7c0add35c56fd4a11f99b2f72e874738b3c22ea7673`, md5 `c9711cca70fdfbdc193c58203d854b07`), written by kai from the image's own `xa.cu` (rgh's; it stays unchanged, with its `xa.cubin`). No other code went into it.
* Built with nvcc 13.4 (`Cuda compilation tools, release 13.4, V13.4.92`, `Build cuda_13.4.r13.4/compiler.38855100_0`) on GPU host #2 on 2026-10-22, compile only, with the build line of the table (the same host rebuilt the shipped `xa.cubin` byte for byte from `xa.cu` in the same directory first: md5 `ffd9b76f...`). `xa3.cubin` sha256 `31cd78d9...`, md5 `8d32bb19788497bb6b73a1be5cce25ac`. No `_INTERNAL_` symbol, so the build path does not matter. A local nvcc 13.0.88 build gives other bytes (as it does for `xa.cu`).
* ptxas (`-Xptxas -v`): `xa_fwd3q` and `xa_fwd3qe` each 128 registers, 72 bytes stack frame, 72 bytes spill stores / loads, 1 barrier: the same 128-register / 72 bytes stack budget as `xa_fwd2q` (the build's kill gate: <= 128 registers, <= 72 bytes stack).
* Kernels: `xa_fwd3q` (late gate + batched Q-build loads, the lever) and `xa_fwd3qe` (late gate only, for attribution); `xa_fwd2q`'s signature, grid, 512 threads and 100352 B dynamic shared memory. What changed against `xa.cu` is only where global loads are issued: the gate tile (32 KB) goes by cp.async into the dead Q tile in the final key block's first V-chunk step and the epilogue reads it from shared memory; the Q-build loads its 4 rows and the position's cos / sin once, before the arithmetic. Every arithmetic line is `xa.cu`'s text (tests/test_xa3.py pins the lines that differ).
* Start-up gate (`xa.variant_check`, inside `PackedForward.check_xa` and `fcl.xl_check`, so also in `ntv.recheck`): on every input the XA / XL gates draw (random decisions with and without the prefix layout, raw-input scales, all 65536 gate values) and on outlier and order-witness inputs (`xa.witness_inputs`), the variant's output against `xa_fwd2q`'s, byte for byte over every row; any miss or error keeps `xa_fwd2q` for that (XA or XL, bucket). FCAB pick lever `xa3` (arms `xa3` / `noxa3`, on `pf.xa_ver` and `pf.xl_ver`); `S1ENG_XA3=1` puts the env lanes on it, `S1ENG_XA3_VER=3qe` picks the attribution kernel.

## onorm.cubin: the build path is part of the output

`onorm.cu` has a device function in an anonymous namespace. nvcc names it `_INTERNAL_<module id>_<n>_<file>_...`, and the module id is the CRC32 of the source file's ABSOLUTE path. So `onorm.cubin` is byte-identical only when it is built from **`/opt/s1eng/s1eng/onorm.cu`** (CRC32 `ecfb0072`, the id in the shipped file). It does not matter whether nvcc gets `onorm.cu` from inside that directory or the absolute path. Built at any other path, only `.strtab`, the string table that holds that name, differs. Every other section is equal, so the machine code is the same. Every other cubin here is path-independent.

`onorm.cu` is rgh's `onorm_v17.cu` (sha256 `ec42b12a08a1278daf8cfac36854b93b38a419e34a1d33cd0941c7e5996cbbd8`). The earlier image #131 shipped `onorm.cubin` `9319aa5e5facc6ae4850e448bab788b9e8644e850047d5dd4166b021e0f36b96`, built from the same source under the name `ffs_on.cu` at a path nobody recorded (module id `d1e37abf`). That file and this one are code-identical: every `.text.*`, `.nv.info*`, constant and `.nv.capmerc` section is byte-equal. Only `.strtab` and the two symbol tables that point into it differ, so this image ships the rebuild from the documented path instead.

## onormpv.cubin (PROFUSE-v, ruj r3; switch `S1ENG_PROFUSE`, default off)

* Source: `onormpv.cu` (sha256 `24b7bbdcb70982893eb7f3c49cff83ae6ef0703bddcdd75cfae31a3f1354eb45`) = `#include "onorm.cu"` (rgh's `onorm.cu`, sha256 `ec42b12a08a1278daf8cfac36854b93b38a419e34a1d33cd0941c7e5996cbbd8`, unchanged: the same file `onorm.cubin` is built from) + the PROFUSE-v section: `ffs_pv5n` = `fused5_body<SKIP, !TIMED, NORM>` with exactly `onorm.cubin`'s flag paths (`ONORM_V=5`, `ONORM_PF2`, `ONORM_SILU_FIN`, `ONORM_FINROLL`) and one change - v is not loaded from the prologue's output but converted in shared memory from the raw packed qkv rows (prefix-variant cache rows below plen), per 64-row chunk at the top of the chunk, with PRON's `conv_tile4` arithmetic op for op (FHFMA 4-tap conv, F9 SiLU, rows >= slen +0); the o tile of chunk i is staged in that chunk's w buffer as in ONORM. `ffs_pvx` (gate helper) runs the same staging + conversion and writes v; `ffs_pv_smem` returns the dynamic shared memory (101120 bytes = ONORM's 99328 + a 768-byte halo + 1024 bytes of conv weights). `onorm.cu`'s own kernels are compiled into this cubin too (unused: the engine loads them from `onorm.cubin`).
* The build path is part of the output, as for `onorm.cubin`: the anonymous-namespace device functions are named after nvcc's module id, the CRC32 of the source's absolute path, so `onormpv.cubin` is byte-identical when built from **`/opt/s1eng/s1eng/onormpv.cu`** (with `onorm.cu` next to it) with the build line above (nvcc 13.4, `V13.4.92`; host compiler irrelevant).
* ptxas (`-Xptxas -v`): `ffs_pv5n` 255 registers, 8 bytes stack frame, 8 bytes spill stores / loads (= `ffs_fused5n`'s), 1 barrier; `ffs_pvx` 118 registers, no spill.
* Dispatch: a packed graph (bucket L, B slots) runs PRON with `qk_only=True` (pron.cu's q / k head blocks and gate units; `pron.cubin` unchanged), KKT2, then `ffs_pv5n` iff `S1ENG_PROFUSE=1`, L passed the gate and ONORM itself would run for (L, B) (L in PRON's and ONORM's buckets, B >= ONORM's bmin); everything else runs as before (PRON full -> KKT2 -> `ffs_fused5n`).
* Start-up gate (`onormpv.check`, in `capture_batch` after ONORM's, and again in `ntv.recheck` at a changed pmax): per bucket, at every B ONORM runs at, random packed layouts with every other GDN layer's conv / gate / norm weights, input scales 1 / 8 / 0.02, unused slots, prefix layouts (none; the template prefix pfx .. pmax over 3 variant blocks; chunk-edge prefixes 1..3 / 62..65 / 126..129), z beside the qkv rows or separate, z with exp-overflow / zero / tiny / -0 values; through BOTH chains, bit for bit: q, k, beta, g, A; the gate kernel's v vs the full prologue's v on every row of every slot; the packed gated-norm output on every real row. Any difference or error keeps that bucket on the unchanged chain.

## Not shipped (compared with #131)

* `ngemm9g.cubin` (rgh's GRP grouped projection GEMMs, `ngg9_*`) has no source, so it is removed together with its plan `plan_grp.json`. `S1ENG_GRP=0` is set in the image, and `model.py` calls `setup_grp` only when `S1ENG_GRP=1`, so nothing opens `ngemm9g.cubin`. `grp.py` stays as inert source. The LATE side-node order (also read from `plan_grp.json`, only inside `setup_grp`) is off with it.
* `ngemm5_sm89.cubin` / `ngemm5_sm90.cubin` (NG3 for sm_89 / sm_90 GPUs) are removed. `ng.py` picks the cubin by compute capability and checks that the file exists, so on sm_120 it loads only `ngemm5.cubin`.

## Notes

* `-Xptxas -v` only prints register use, but ptxas writes its own command line into the cubin's `.note.nv.tkinfo` section. Without the flag the machine code is the same and that note differs, so the file differs.
* The output does not depend on the host compiler. The same 14 files came out of nvcc 13.4.92 with g++ 13.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 container, `--network none`) and with g++ 15.2 (Ubuntu 26.04).
* Check: copy this directory to `/opt/s1eng/s1eng` (a container or a private mount namespace), run the build lines and compare with `sha256sum *.cubin`.

## ngemm7.cubin: the from-source rebuild

NG7 (S1ENG_NG7=1, S1ENG_NG7_TABLE=1) is added on top of #137. `ngemm7.cubin` here is rebuilt from `ngemm7.cu` with the build line above. Compared with the cubin r1_ng7 shipped, every `.text.*` section and the whole SASS (29526 lines) are equal; only `.note.nv.tkinfo` (the toolkit's record of the nvcc command line) differs, so the machine code is the same and this image ships the documented rebuild.
